verdict_policy: Archives retain their confirmed-malware verdicts. Each of the six listed extracted members was judged independently from its bytes.
changes: Two additive notable file-I/O observations. No existing matcher, criticality, description or consumer was weakened or removed. Recursive YAML-reference inspection found no ancestor-directory consumers of either new leaf selector.

tests.result: 24 assertions passed across 8 static benign/near-miss controls; no suspicious/hostile findings on these controls.

members.marker_note: parser-session writer: steals env and evaluates HTTP replies
members.identification: Hex-obfuscated exfiltration and response-evaluation function in parser-session 1.1.9
path_trace: On module loading it imports os and ../package.json and constructs a data object by spreading all process.env values alongside platform, hostname, username, package subModuleVersion and noninternal IPv4-interface MAC addresses.

The local g() decoder parses two hex characters at a time with radix 16 and String.fromCharCode. The table resolves to require, axios, post, an HTTPS endpoint, headers, x-secret-header, secret and then.

Invoking the exported arrow function calls axios.post(endpoint, data, headerOptions). The response callback executes eval(r.data); its catch handler swallows failures. The require table entry at index 0 is unused.
members.verdict_basis: Bulk environment export and execution of remotely supplied response code are concealed in a parser/logging-shaped package with no purpose requiring either behavior.
limits: No particular credential value in process.env is established.

The archive lacks src/package.json required by this member, and its entrypoint references an unbundled .pnpm/httpreslog path rather than this local member. Ordinary loading may therefore fail; these defects do not make the implemented exfiltration/evaluation behavior benign.
The remote response was not fetched or evaluated.

members.marker_note: osinthell v.js: silent recursive deletion of System32 DLLs
members.identification: osinthell 1.6.9 exported Windows system-DLL deletion action
path_trace: require(child_process) binds execSync. Its exported zero-argument function invokes del /F /S /Q C:\Windows\System32\*.dll with shell:true and stdio:ignore, swallowing errors.
The package index imports the function as v and calls it unconditionally from the exported sorgu() routine, alongside other destructive actions.
members.verdict_basis: An unattended recursive forced deletion of OS DLLs has no coherent OSINT utility purpose.
limits: Runtime invocation, required permissions and which DLLs would survive locks/ACLs are unknown.
members.hostile_goal: One destructive objective is supported. No additional distinct hostile action occurs in this tiny member. Silent stdio, error suppression and shell invocation are already retained as notable capabilities; they do not justify extra hostile traits.
members.classifier_disagreement: All routed models return cls=0; calibrated level remains -1 and the standalone scan exits 0 despite hostile static findings. This is a classifier gap, not a reason to alter accurate traits. The scanner also warns that model feature version 18 predates expected version 21.

members.marker_note: osinthell f.js: zeroes physical disk boot sector and partition table
members.identification: osinthell 1.6.9 exported Windows boot-sector wiper with bootrec invocation
path_trace: The export opens \\.\PhysicalDrive0 in r+ mode, allocates 512 zero bytes, writes all 512 at disk offset zero and closes the handle, suppressing errors.
It separately invokes bootrec /fixmbr via child_process.execSync with shell:true and stdio:ignore. This repair command cannot recover the erased partition table.
The package index imports the function as f and calls it unconditionally from sorgu().
members.verdict_basis: It deliberately zeroes a hardcoded physical disk boot sector, including its partition table, without a user-selected disk or supplied replacement data.
limits: Raw-disk access generally needs elevation; success was not observed. bootrec is a legitimate repair primitive and remains notable rather than a separate hostile behavior.
members.hostile_goal: One disk-destruction objective is supported. Handle open/write, zero-fill and the separate boot-record repair call are covered; adding multiple hostile labels would duplicate the same write or misclassify repair.
members.classifier_disagreement: All routed models return cls=0; calibrated level remains -1 and the standalone scan exits 0 despite hostile static findings. This is a classifier gap, not a reason to alter accurate traits. The scanner also warns that model feature version 18 predates expected version 21.

members.marker_note: osinthell p.js: silently truncates files at four drive roots
path_trace: The export enumerates C:\, D:\, E:\ and F:\ using fs.readdirSync. For each direct child it joins the path, checks fs.statSync(...).isFile() and calls fs.writeFileSync(full, "") in the default destructive mode.
Nested catches suppress enumeration, metadata and write errors. The operation visits root entries; it does not recursively walk directories or securely erase data.
The package index imports the function as p and calls it unconditionally from sorgu().
members.verdict_basis: It indiscriminately empties existing files on multiple hardcoded drive roots, unrelated to OSINT or an ordinary cleanup task.
limits: Only writable files are affected; no successful execution was observed.
members.hostile_goal: Two retained hostile composites corroborate the same truncation objective. The file contains no third distinct hostile behavior; filesystem enumeration, stat and empty-write primitives are already covered.
members.classifier_disagreement: All routed models return cls=0; calibrated level remains -1 and the standalone scan exits 0 despite hostile static findings. This is a classifier gap, not a reason to alter accurate traits. The scanner also warns that model feature version 18 predates expected version 21.

members.marker_note: osinthell t.js: silently disables boot recovery and failure handling
path_trace: The export calls child_process.execSync for bcdedit /set {default} bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures, followed by bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled No. Both specify shell:true and stdio:ignore. A shared empty catch suppresses errors; failure of the first call can skip the second.
The package index imports the function as t and calls it unconditionally from sorgu().
members.verdict_basis: A silent zero-argument action disables recovery and boot-failure handling within an ostensibly OSINT utility, reinforcing sabotage rather than interactive administration.
limits: Elevation and successful BCD modification were not observed. Generic bcdedit commands remain suspicious/notable because they are also administrative operations.
members.hostile_goal: Both commands implement one recovery-sabotage objective. No independent persistence, theft or command-channel behavior is present in this member. Extra hostile traits would count the same outcome repeatedly.

This is a classifier gap, not a reason to alter accurate traits. The scanner also warns that model feature version 18 predates expected version 21.

members.marker_note: Installer: credential theft, upload, persistence; add shell file I/O
members.identification: Universal x86_64/arm64 C++ launcher for an obfuscated macOS credential stealer
path_trace: Both entry points construct a decrypted string, obtain its C string, and pass it to system().

The __const blob starts with seed 0x11667. Each byte is XORed with the low state byte, then state = (state * 0x3785 mod 2^32) mod 35999. The modulus is derived from the embedded time 09:59:59. Manual decryption agrees exactly with cleave facts; identical encrypted payloads occur in both architectures.
The 37076-byte command invokes osascript and evaluates return-joined AppleScript. The final call reaches the main handler.

The main handler validates a cached password with dscl . authonly, otherwise repeatedly prompts for a hidden password under an Installation pretext. It records the password locally and in a randomized /tmp staging directory.

File-copy handlers read input and run cat with quoted input/output paths; other handlers truncate/write files, recursively copy selected stores, and use Finder duplication for Safari, Notes and personal files. Targets include Chromium logins/cookies, Firefox key4.db/logins.json, Keychains, desktop/extension wallets, Notes and extension-filtered Desktop/Documents files.
The staging directory is compressed with ditto into /tmp/out.zip, uploaded by curl --data-binary with campaign/account headers, and the ZIP and directory are removed.
A handler downloads a Ledger Live ZIP, kills the existing application, removes it via password-fed sudo and extracts the replacement into /Applications.

Another handler fetches shell text and embeds it in a KeepAlive/RunAtLoad LaunchDaemon using /bin/bash -c. It copies/bootstrap-loads the plist via sudo -S. On bootstrap error the fetched command is passed to nohup.
members.verdict_basis: Password deception, targeted secret collection, external upload, wallet replacement and persistence collectively establish malicious intent from the member itself.
limits: No payload was executed; successful theft, privilege use, download or installation was not observed.
The fetched wallet replacement and shell response are not contained in this member; their final contents are unknown.
Packaging postinstall disables Gatekeeper/removes quarantine, but those are sibling-script behaviors and were not attributed to this member.

controlled_comparison.method: Snapshot of git HEAD rules versus current rules, same member/CLI, CLEAVE_SKIP_CACHE=1. Snapshot is kept under scratch/stranded-analysis/original-traits.
controlled_comparison.explanation: Initial cached native report and subsequent standalone reports differed in architecture/neutral derived findings. Identical uncached original/current scans both reproduce the smaller set, demonstrating that the YAML additions did not cause those differences. The archive comparison also retains all preexisting findings.
